derivation: fragrouter-1.6 rebuilt with that block applied, so the attack is analyzable as the archive a victim would have unpacked.

reconstruction.direction: The block published as the fragroute-1.2 backdoor, applied forward to the clean fragrouter-1.6 tarball.

insertion_point.anchor: immediately after the -lsocket check closes, before the net/ethernet.h header test
insertion_point.reasoning: Two constraints agree on this point and no source states it. The block's own compile line is `gcc $LIBS conftest.c`, so it has to run after the socket library check has put -lsocket into $LIBS or the payload would not link where socket() lives outside libc; and the fragroute-1.2 copy, the one position that was published, sits at exactly this relative point, immediately after its socket/nsl checks and before the next test.

packaging.normalized: member mtime, uid/gid and owner names zeroed; gzip mtime 0
packaging.framing: ustar, REGTYPE; reproduces the fragroute-1.2 reconstruction byte for byte from its own inputs
